claims.text: Alloying a high-entropy alloy with elements having significantly different atomic radii introduces lattice distortions.
Phonon scattering caused by lattice distortions reduces phonon thermal conductivity.
The intervention will produce lower phonon thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable untreated high-entropy alloy.
The predicted reduction applies from 300 K to 1000 K at 1 atm.
The predicted reduction applies while the material is solid.
The proposed intervention applies to high-entropy alloys in either the as-cast or solution-treated state.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-flash analysis can be used to evaluate the intervention's effect on phonon thermal conductivity.
Failure to observe a significantly lower phonon thermal conductivity in the alloyed specimen would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention adds alloying elements, whereas the baseline is described as having the same composition but without those elements. Removing or omitting added elements necessarily changes the composition, so the stated control cannot simultaneously be compositionally identical and lack the alloying elements.
